reviews.comment: There's definitely worse professors out there(maybe not for 229). Her lectures are okayish, but she genuinely can't answer the most simple questions so don't get lost. Other than that, the exams are very similar to the practice exams, and she's a very kind and caring person overall.

follows notes from another prof in class, not great at answering questions but shes really nice & wants students to do well. there are lots of resources to do well in this class but people do not take advantage of them so they do poorly. i read textbook on my own time which helped a lot. shes a good prof overall, acct 229 prof options are very slim

Extremely bad at explaining topics to students, consistently has circular explanations that make you feel like you shouldn't have even asked. I would have to attend other accounting 229 classes to properly understand. A nice lady in general, but it was extremely difficult to understand unless you were talking about something that wasn't complex.
No matter how much you study, it's hard to do well in this class unless you just attend a different professors lectures.

I'll be honest, I can't disagree with a lot of what people say about Professor McGowan. In my opinion, she's a very kind person, generally, but the disparity between Knoop and her test averages was usually around 10 points. Looking back, if I had to do it again, I'd attend Knoop's lectures instead. Also, I would check for exam grading mistakes.

It is very important to attend lectures in ACCT 229 as you get to interact and engage with the professor in class. She is always open to questions and tries her best to answer them. She is also very friendly and helpful during office hours. It is easy to get an A in ACCT 229 if you attend class and diligently do the extra problems provided.

Going into this class I knew it would be difficult. Her lectures are laughable. This is the first semester of her teaching this course and it shows. She goes through a notes packet from Knoop and copies directly from it, with no explanation supporting what she is "teaching". Just avoid her as a teacher. Test avg was 17 pts lower than other classes.

Ms McGowan failed one of my assignments because she said I did not attend the event that was required. I did attend the event. Not only did she refuse to work with me to prove my attendance, but she was also incredibly rude and dismissive during the (two-week long) email exchange that we had regarding the assignment.

This was an easy class made harder by her inability to grade properly. There were a couple assignments I received bad grades on because of her errors, which were eventually fixed, only after constant followup due to her delayed responses. Also, for a class all about recruiting & getting internships/jobs, she was not very encouraging or excited.
Confusing lectures. She also is not very understanding.

Prof McGowan is a kind human, but not a good teacher. I had a very hard time following her lectures, as did my peers. I DO NOT recommend taking her for ACCT 230. She communicates the material poorly and confuses students. I had to teach myself the material outside of class. She also assigns a massive group project toward the end of the semester.

She is really great. She tells funny stories during class and really wants to get to know everyone. Her tests are just like the practice tests, so if you can do them then you will be fine. The group project is annoying, but it's not that hard, and she grades it pretty easily. I loved her and would take a class with her again!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: PLEASE do not take her. It is a known fact of Mays not to take a McGowan ACCT course. I took ACCT 229 once and passed with a B. Test are unreasonably tough and she assigns an incredibly stressful group project where you have to build an entire company from the bottom up. Also there's no outside tutor for this class so good luck learning on your own
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I had her as my Honors Acct 230 professor and I very much regret taking this class as an honors course. Your grade mostly consists of exams, which are difficult, and a project, which is VERY time-consuming. Her teaching methods were all over the place and usually fast-paced. It was difficult to really grasp the material, even after asking questions

Attendance isn't mandatory, but I strongly suggest going to class. She sometimes has difficulty explaining the material to students and works fairly fast, but is willing to slow down and explain further. She is entertaining in class, and enjoys talking to students. Tests aren't too hard if you do the online practice problems. Should be an A or a B.

I took McGowan for Honors Accounting 230. I often had a hard time following her in class. Be prepared to teach yourself outside of class. That being said, she's really nice and funny. She makes sure that there's a certain level of As and Bs in her classes so don't be too worried about making the grades if you don't do well on the first test.
